reviews.title: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
reviews.explanation: The application does not set the X-Content-Type-Options header on responses. The source excerpt shows no code that adds this header, and a runtime probe (zap.10021) observed a GET request to '/' without the header, confirming its absence in practice.
reviews.impact: Without the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header, browsers may perform MIME type sniffing, potentially allowing content injection attacks such as cross-site scripting (XSS) when malicious content is served with an incorrect MIME type.
reviews.remediation: Configure the FastAPI application to include the X-Content-Type-Options header on all responses, e.g., using a middleware that adds `response.headers['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff'`.
evidence: Source excerpt shows no header being set (lines 161-166).
Runtime probe fact (zap.10021) reports a GET request to '/' with the header missing.

reviews.title: Job listing requires admin role
reviews.explanation: The endpoint /admin/jobs calls a function principal(authorization) before accessing the database, but the provided source excerpt does not show any role verification or access control logic that ensures the caller has an admin role. The runtime probe observed a successful 200 response when accessing the endpoint, whereas the scanner expected a 403 or 404, indicating that the access control may be missing or ineffective.
reviews.impact: An unauthenticated or non‑admin user could retrieve the full list of jobs, potentially exposing sensitive internal data and enabling further attacks such as data leakage or enumeration of job identifiers.
reviews.remediation: Implement proper role‑based access control in the principal function or directly in the admin_jobs handler, ensuring that only users with an admin role can access this endpoint. Return 403 for unauthorized requests.
evidence: Source excerpt shows admin_jobs calls principal(authorization) but no visible role check
Runtime probe fact: GET /admin/jobs returned status 200, while expected 403/404
limitations: The implementation of principal() is not provided, so it cannot be confirmed whether it performs adequate admin role verification
No additional scanner evidence beyond the single runtime probe is available to independently corroborate the missing check

reviews.title: Demoted administrator retains access to admin endpoint
reviews.explanation: The source code defines the /admin/token-report endpoint and checks that the caller's role is "admin", raising HTTP 403 otherwise. However, a runtime probe for this endpoint returned HTTP 200, indicating the role check was bypassed or ineffective, allowing a demoted administrator to access the endpoint despite the intended restriction.
reviews.impact: An attacker who previously held administrative privileges can continue to access privileged functionality after demotion, potentially exposing sensitive data or performing unauthorized actions.
reviews.remediation: Ensure that role information is reliably refreshed after demotion and that the token validation logic correctly reflects the current user role. Invalidate existing tokens on role change and re‑evaluate the role check before granting access.
evidence: Source code shows role check and 403 response for non‑admin users (lines 661‑664).
Runtime probe fact: GET /admin/token-report returned status 200 instead of the expected 403 (workflow.stale_role.3).
